_comments._: Keys starting with _ are stripped by scripts/sync-vapi.ts. ${VAR} placeholders are filled at sync time; {{...}} / {% %} are Vapi Liquid.
_comments.model: Starts from the Balanced preset's model tier: gpt-4.1. Latency tuning: gpt-4.1-mini (faster, weaker at multi-step tool use; try it once the scenario tests pass), gpt-4o-mini (fastest/cheapest, least reliable with 8 tools). Pin a dated snapshot (e.g. gpt-4.1-2025-04-14) to avoid silent model updates. Temperature 0.5 (Vapi's default) for a warmer, less repetitive delivery; tool-call accuracy comes from the backend rules, not low temperature.
_comments.transcriber: Deepgram nova-3 uses keyterm (plain phrases, no boosts; case and punctuation are kept, so 'A/C' is sent as-is). Deepgram allows up to 100 terms / 500 tokens and suggests the most important 20-50; prune place and brand names first if accuracy drops. For lower end-of-turn latency try model flux-general-en.
_comments.voice: Provider and voiceId are a placeholder until the owner picks one (see README 'Voice options'). Vapi voices: version '2' is the newer, more natural model (Emma, Clara, Savannah support it). speed is 0.25-2 for Vapi. chunkPlan: TTS gets whole sentences (no comma boundaries) so speech doesn't sound choppy; minCharacters 30 is Vapi's default. fillerInjectionEnabled no longer exists in Vapi's API, so it isn't set.
_comments.startSpeakingPlan: onNumberSeconds is longer so callers can pause while reading phone numbers, ZIPs and Queens house numbers without being cut off. Lower waitSeconds (0.4) for snappier turns.
_comments.stopSpeakingPlan: numWords 2 means 'uh-huh' doesn't interrupt the assistant; a real interruption of 2+ words does.
_comments.hooks: Idle messages via customer.speech.timeout hooks (replaces the older messagePlan.idleMessages).
_comments.analysisPlan: Deprecated in the API but still works; feeds message.analysis.summary into our calls table. Migrate to structured outputs later.
_comments.firstMessage: Never personalized: callers aren't verified at greeting time. assistant-request (ASSISTANT_REQUEST_ENABLED) only sets caller_recognized, used by the prompt. Vapi has no first-message delay for inbound calls (checked Oct 2026), so the opening words 'Hi, thanks for calling' are deliberately skippable if the line clips them.
_comments.firstMessageInterruptionsEnabled: false (Vapi's default): the caller's 'hello?' while the line connects doesn't cut the greeting off.
_comments.serverMessages: status-update is for keep-warm: on status 'in-progress' /api/vapi/events runs a non-blocking select 1 so a suspended production database wakes during the greeting, not on the first tool call. Other statuses are ignored.

name: Summit Air Virtual Assistant
firstMessage: Hi, thanks for calling Summit Air! This is Ava, the virtual assistant. What's going on today?

exact: I'm still here whenever you're ready.

endCallMessage: Thanks for calling Summit Air. Take care.

messages.content: Summarize this Summit Air HVAC call for the office in 2-3 sentences: who called, the problem, urgency, and the outcome (booked window, priority dispatch, callback, safety stop, or nothing). Note anything the office must follow up on.
